svg.title: Conflict detection in Egres: after locking its rows a statement checks the oracle for the highest commit timestamp among them, and bumps the transaction read timestamp to it instead of aborting when the earlier reads still hold
svg.desc: Transaction T1 begins with read timestamp 1020. Its first statement locks row r7, whose last commit at 1010 is below the snapshot, so it proceeds. Another transaction commits r8 at 1038. T1's second statement locks r8 and finds the commit at 1038 above its snapshot, so the rows are stale. The oracle confirms that r7, read by the first statement, has not moved, so the read timestamp is bumped from 1020 to 1038, the locks stay held, and only the second statement re-runs. T1 commits at 1042 through Raft with no validation at commit.

text.font-family: 'JetBrains Mono', ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, Consolas, monospace

svg.text: EGRES · CONFLICT DETECTION · BUMPING A STATEMENT'S READ TIMESTAMP INSTEAD OF ABORTING
